notes: The Liao fell in 1125; the Jurchen Jin ruled north China.
Iraq was ruled by the revived Abbasid Caliphate.
The Buyids ended in 1062; Iran was contested by the Khwarazmians.
The Fatimids ended in 1171; Egypt and Syria were Ayyubid.
The Ghaznavids fell in 1186 to the Ghurids.
Delhi was held by Ghurid generals until the Sultanate formed in 1206.
The Mongol Empire was proclaimed in 1206; in 1200 Temüjin was uniting the tribes.
Ifat replaced the Sultanate of Shewa only in 1285.
The Buyids ended in 1062.
Northern India: Ghurid conquests to Bihar; the Deccan was divided among the Yadavas, Kakatiyas and Hoysalas.
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Corrected (AP review): Castile and Aragon held Toledo, Madrid, Cuenca and Zaragoza; the Almohad frontier ran south of the Tagus.
Corrected (AP review): central Anatolia was the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum; the crusader states (Jerusalem from Acre, Tripoli, Antioch), Armenian Cilicia and Zagwe Ethiopia are now drawn.
The Moche culture ended about 800; the north coast is the Sicán (Lambayeque) culture.
The Nile and the Horn of Africa are named for their peoples and states of the time.
The Caribbean islands were settled from about 5000 BCE (the Bahamas from about 700 CE): Archaic peoples, then the Saladoid peoples and the Taíno.
Peoples who formed in the colonial era are replaced by the peoples who lived there before 1500.
Andean and Amazonian peoples are named for their time.
North American cultures are named for their time; the Mississippi and Ohio valleys were the land of the Mississippian and Fort Ancient cultures (boxes approximate).
